questions.question_text:
The raw test scores of $11$ students are given:
$6, 6, 7, 7, 7, 8, 8, 8, 8, 9, 9$
When organised into a frequency table, what is the frequency of the score $8$?

options.why: States the score value itself instead of counting its frequency.
Miscounts the occurrences of score $8$ by counting $7$s instead.
States the total number of observations rather than the frequency of $8$.

questions.solution_text:
The score $8$ appears $4$ times in the dataset.
$\text{Frequency of } 8 = 4$

questions.question_text:
A frequency table is shown below:
$\begin{array}{c|c} x & f \\ \hline 2 & 5 \\ 3 & 8 \\ 4 & 9 \\ 5 & 3 \end{array}$
What is the cumulative frequency ($cf$) for the score $4$?

options.why: States the individual frequency of score $4$ instead of the running total.
Sums only the first two frequencies $5 + 8$ without including the frequency of $4$.
Sums all frequencies in the table instead of stopping at score $4$.

questions.question_text:
The table shows the frequency distribution of shoe sizes in a store.
$\begin{array}{c|c} \text{Size }(x) & \text{Frequency }(f) \\ \hline 7 & 4 \\ 8 & 11 \\ 9 & 18 \\ 10 & 9 \\ 11 & 3 \end{array}$
What is the mode of the shoe sizes?

options.why: States the highest frequency instead of the corresponding shoe size.
Selects the second most frequent score instead of the maximum.
Calculates the mean of the distribution (rounded to one decimal place) instead of identifying the mode.

questions.solution_text:
The highest frequency is $18$, which corresponds to size $9$.
$\text{Mode} = 9$

questions.question_text:
A survey of $25$ people recorded the number of cars per household.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c} x & f & cf \\ \hline 1 & 3 & 3 \\ 2 & 6 & 9 \\ 3 & 8 & 17 \\ 4 & 5 & 22 \\ 5 & 3 & 25 \end{array}$
What is the median number of cars?

options.why: Calculates half of $25$ without finding the score on the table.
Selects the score where cumulative frequency is $9$, which is less than $13$.
States the frequency of the median score instead of the score itself.

questions.question_text:
Calculate the mean $\overline{x}$ for the following discrete frequency distribution:
$\begin{array}{c|c} x & f \\ \hline 0 & 4 \\ 1 & 6 \\ 2 & 8 \\ 3 & 2 \end{array}$

options.why: Averages the score values $(0+1+2+3)/4$ without weighting by frequency.
States the sum of products $\Sigma xf$ without dividing by the total frequency $20$.
Divides $\Sigma xf = 28$ by $24$ instead of the correct $\Sigma f = 20$.

questions.question_text:
The table shows the number of typographical errors per page in a book of $40$ sample pages.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{Errors }(x) & \text{Frequency }(f) & cf \\ \hline 0 & 6 & 6 \\ 1 & 12 & 18 \\ 2 & 14 & 32 \\ 3 & 5 & 37 \\ 4 & 3 & 40 \end{array}$
How many pages had **at most $2$** errors?

options.why: States the frequency of exactly $2$ errors rather than 'at most $2$'.
Counts pages with fewer than $2$ errors (only $0$ and $1$ errors).
Counts pages with more than $2$ errors ($40 - 32 = 8$).

questions.solution_text:
'At most $2$' means $x \le 2$.
From the cumulative frequency column at $x = 2$, $cf = 32$.
$32\text{ pages}$

questions.question_text:
A survey of $35$ participants recorded scores in the table below, with one missing frequency $m$.
$\begin{array}{c|c} x & f \\ \hline 10 & 7 \\ 20 & 14 \\ 30 & m \\ 40 & 5 \end{array}$
Find the value of $m$ and the relative frequency of the score $30$ as a fraction.

options.why: Divides $m$ by the sum of the known frequencies, $7+14+5=26$, instead of the total $35$.
Leaves the last frequency $5$ out of the sum, giving $m = 35 - (7+14) = 14$.
Leaves the frequency $5$ out of the sum AND divides by the known-frequency total $26$, making both slips at once.

questions.question_text:
The table shows the distribution of scores for $45$ students.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c} x & f & cf \\ \hline 11 & 5 & 5 \\ 12 & 9 & 14 \\ 13 & 16 & 30 \\ 14 & 10 & 40 \\ 15 & 5 & 45 \end{array}$
What is the median score?

options.why: States the median position $Mp = \frac{45+1}{2} = 23$ instead of the score.
Selects the score where $cf = 14$, which is below the median position of $23$.
Selects $x = 14$ where $cf = 40$, which is past the first score exceeding $23$.

questions.question_text:
Dave recorded the number of pets his classmates have in the frequency table: 0 pets has frequency 2, 1 has 5, 2 has 3, 3 has 6, and 4 has 4.
How many people did Dave record the results of?

options.why: Adds only part of the listed frequencies.
Counts categories rather than people.
Counts table rows rather than the total frequency.

questions.solution_text: Add all frequencies: $2+5+3+6+4=20$. Therefore Dave recorded 20 classmates.

questions.question_text:
Pedro conducts a survey to find out how many pens his classmates have in their pencil case today.
The results are on the right.
Pedro forgot to ask Sally, who has 3 pens.
Which box will change in value when Sally is included?
The table gives numbers of pens 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 with frequencies 2, 4, 7, 5 and 3 respectively.

options.why: The category value remains three pens when another observation is added.

options.text: B: the frequency 5 for three pens

options.why: Sally has three pens, so the category four is not affected.

options.text: D: the frequency 3 for four pens
options.why: The frequency for four pens changes only when someone has four pens.

questions.solution_text: Sally has 3 pens, so the frequency for the category 3 increases from 5 to 6. Therefore box B changes value.
